item.title: Are U.S. Operations in Venezuela a Blueprint for China for Taiwan?
item.description: CSIS and Taiwan experts react to the U.S. operation in Venezuela’s implications for China and how it affects Beijing’s calculus on Taiwan.

item.title: Measures Short of Invasion
item.description: China has significantly increased pressure on Taiwan in recent years, stoking fears that it could invade the island.

item.title: Why the Golden Fleet Will Sail
item.description: Debates over a new battleship miss the larger issue—how to generate affordable naval firepower at scale. Seen as an arsenal ship, a “Golden Fleet” could reinforce distributed maritime operations while helping reform U.S. shipbuilding.

item.title: Why Losing Local Voices in Foreign Aid–Diplomacy Mergers Threatens National Security
item.description: Merging USAID’s functions with those of the State Department could weaken U.S. foreign policy, potentially reducing local input in the policymaking process and eroding access, context, and long-term relationships.

item.title: What the Bella-1 Teaches Us About Targeting Shadow Fleets
item.description: After a globe-spanning chase, the United States seized a sanctioned oil tanker tied to Iran and Venezuela. What does the Bella-1 reveal about shadow fleets, AIS manipulation, and how maritime interdiction is reshaping sanctions enforcement?

item.title: CSIS Middle East Program Names Vali Nasr as Non-Resident Senior Adviser and Joseph Farsakh as Non-Resident Senior Associate
item.description: The Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) today announced the appointments of Vali Nasr as non-resident senior adviser and Joseph Farsakh as non-resident senior associate with the CSIS Middle East Program.

item.title: SCOTUS Ruling and Korea
item.description: The Supreme Court’s ruling on the consolidated cases of V.O.S. Selections, Inc. v. Trump and Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump is expected tomorrow. Here are some key numbers to keep in mind with this impending decision.

item.title: U.S.-India Insight: Beyond Optics: India’s New Strategic-Commercial Linkages
item.description: As global alignments shift, India is quietly deepening trade and security ties with U.S. allies—even as high-profile engagements with rivals grab headlines. A closer look shows substance, not symbolism, is shaping India’s strategic direction.

item.title: From Regime Change to Regime Management: Washington’s Venezuela Strategy
item.description: CSIS Americas Deputy Director and Senior Fellow Christopher Hernandez-Roy analyzes future directions for Venezuela following the capture of Nicolás Maduro.
